docs.text: HardFOC driver Vortex Driver ¶ A C++20 CANopen host client for HardFOC Vortex devices. It builds NMT and expedited SDO download frames with named CiA 301 and CiA 402 objects and hands them to a CAN transport you provide, on any MCU or a PC. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it an object with one method, send() , that puts a classic CAN frame on the bus; it does the CANopen encoding: COB-IDs, command specifiers, little-endian payloads. It has no heap, no threads and no dependency on CANopenNode, ESP-IDF or the HardFOC HAL. The device on the other end of the bus Vortex V1 HardFOC MCU ESP32-C6 with a TWAI (classic CAN) controller CAN TWAI TX GPIO14, RX GPIO15, external transceiver; 500 kbit/s in the Vortex V1 HAL Motor control TMC9660 smart gate driver with on-chip FOC CANopen role Server (slave), with CANopenNode from the HAL's third_party/ ; its object dictionary is authoritative This driver The client side: NMT commands and expedited SDO downloads to a node ID Vortex V1 HAL · Pin map What you get ¶ NMT in one call. sendNmt() with NmtCommand::Start , Stop , PreOperational , ResetNode or ResetCommunication , to one node or all. See API guide . Expedited SDO writes. sdoDownloadExpedited() writes 1, 2 or 4 bytes to any index and sub-index, with the CiA 301 command specifier for the size. See API guide . Named objects. Controlword, statusword, modes of operation, position and velocity actual value, error register and a HardFOC vendor range. See Hardware . Any CAN driver. One virtual method to implement; a BaseCan adapter is ten lines. See Porting . Checked bytes. The code on these pages is compiled and run on the host against a loopback transport that compares every frame. See Testing and CI . Transmit only The session sends requests and does not read the bus: no SDO responses or uploads, no PDOs, heartbeats or EMCY. Read those with your CAN driver, hf-utils-canopen or CANopenNode. API guide lists what to use for each. Where to go next ¶ Quickstart Wire the bus, write the transport, start a node. Hardware Bus settings, COB-IDs, frame layouts, objects. API guide NMT, SDO and the CiA 402 state machine.

docs.text: API guide ¶ Send NMT commands, write objects and walk a drive through the CiA 402 state machine, with code that compiles and is checked byte for byte. The shape of the API ¶ Everything is in namespace hf::vortex ; include vortex/VortexHostSession.hpp (it includes the others). Type What it is VortexHostSession The client: sendNmt() , sdoDownloadExpedited() , transport() VortexCanTransport The interface you implement: bool send(const VortexCanFrame&) VortexCanFrame id , dlc , extended , rtr , data[8] , pad() NmtCommand NMT command bytes ( VortexProtocol.hpp ) kIdx* , kSub* Object indices ( table ) Every call returns bool : true when your transport accepted the frame. Nothing waits for the node. Create a session ¶ hf :: vortex :: VortexHostSession session ( transport ); // transport: your VortexCanTransport The session stores a reference: keep the transport alive as long as the session. It is cheap to create one per use. NMT ¶ sendNmt(command, node) sends a two-byte NMT frame. Node 0 addresses every node on the bus. bool reset_and_start_all ( VortexHostSession & session ) { constexpr std :: uint8_t kAllNodes = 0 ; // NMT broadcast return session . sendNmt ( NmtCommand :: ResetCommunication , kAllNodes ) && session . sendNmt ( NmtCommand :: Start , kAllNodes ); } Command Node goes to NmtCommand::Start Operational: PDOs run NmtCommand::Stop Stopped: only NMT and heartbeat NmtCommand::PreOperational Pre-operational: SDO works, PDOs do not NmtCommand::ResetNode Full application reset, then boot-up NmtCommand::ResetCommunication Communication objects reset, then boot-up Write an object (SDO download) ¶ sdoDownloadExpedited(node, index, sub, value, size) writes size bytes (1, 2 or 4) of value , low byte first. Any other size returns false without sending. bool write_objects ( VortexHostSession & session , std :: uint8_t node ) { // 1 byte: modes of operation 0x6060:00 = 1 (profile position) if ( ! session . sdoDownloadExpedited ( node , kIdxModesOfOperation , 0 , 1 , 1 )) return false ; // 2 bytes: controlword 0x6040:00 = 0x0006 (CiA 402 Shutdown) if ( ! session . sdoDownloadExpedited ( node , kIdxControlword , 0 , 0x0006 , 2 )) return false ; // 4 bytes: vendor device id 0x2000:01 (placeholder index, see the protocol table) return session . sdoDownloadExpedited ( node , kIdxVendorDeviceId , kSubVendorDeviceId , 0xCAFE0001u , 4 ); } Use the size of the object's data type in the EDS: UNSIGNED8 / INTEGER8 1, UNSIGNED16 / INTEGER16 2, UNSIGNED32 / INTEGER32 4. Pass negative values as their two's-complement bit pattern. Enable a CiA 402 drive ¶ A CiA 402 drive moves through its power state machine when you write commands to the controlword ( 0x6040 ) and reports its state in the statusword ( 0x6041 ): stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> SwitchOnDisabled: power on, initialisation SwitchOnDisabled --> ReadyToSwitchOn: Shutdown 0x0006 ReadyToSwitchOn --> SwitchedOn: Switch on 0x0007 SwitchedOn --> OperationEnabled: Enable operation 0x000F OperationEnabled --> SwitchedOn: Disable operation 0x0007 OperationEnabled --> QuickStopActive: Quick stop 0x0002 QuickStopActive --> SwitchOnDisabled: Disable voltage 0x0000 OperationEnabled --> Fault: fault Fault --> SwitchOnDisabled: Fault reset 0x0080 Disable voltage ( 0x0000 ) also returns Ready to switch on and Switched on to Switch on disabled. // CiA 402 controlword commands (CiA 402 part 2, controlword 0x6040). constexpr std :: uint16_t kCwShutdown = 0x0006 ; // -> Ready to switch on constexpr std :: uint16_t kCwSwitchOn = 0x0007 ; // -> Switched on constexpr std :: uint16_t kCwEnableOperation = 0x000F ; // -> Operation enabled constexpr std :: uint16_t kCwFaultReset = 0x0080 ; // Fault -> Switch on disabled (rising edge of bit 7) bool enable_drive ( VortexHostSession & session , std :: uint8_t node ) { for ( std :: uint16_t cw : { kCwFaultReset , kCwShutdown , kCwSwitchOn , kCwEnableOperation }) { if ( ! session . sdoDownloadExpedited ( node , kIdxControlword , 0 , cw , 2 )) { return false ; } // The session sends only: confirm each state in the statusword (0x6041) with your // own SDO upload or a TPDO before sending the next command. } return true ; } Select the mode of operation ( 0x6060 ) before enabling: 1 profile position, 3 profile velocity, 4 profile torque, 6 homing, 8 / 9 / 10 cyclic synchronous position / velocity / torque, as far as the device supports them. What the session does not do ¶ Need Use SDO response or abort, expedited SDO upload (read an object) Your CAN receive path with CanOpen::ParseSdoResponse() from CanOpenExtras.h in hf-utils-canopen Drive state from the statusword CanOpen::DecodeStatusWord() and CanOpen::NextControlWord() in the same header Heartbeat, EMCY CanOpen::ParseHeartbeat() , CanOpen::ParseEmergency() in the same header Segmented or block SDO (more than 4 bytes), PDO, SYNC A CANopen stack (CANopenNode); configure the node's PDO mapping with SDO writes Retries and timeouts Your application: the session sends once Next: Porting .

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is put together: three layers, one of them yours, and what happens on one call. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application calls a VortexHostSession (its public methods are listed from inc/vortex/VortexHostSession.hpp). The session encodes CANopen NMT and expedited SDO download frames as VortexCanFrame values and hands each to the VortexCanTransport interface (its pure-virtual methods are listed from inc/vortex/VortexCanTransport.hpp). Your transport class implements that interface with BaseCan, SocketCAN or a test loopback, and puts the frame on a classic CAN bus. The Vortex device on the bus is the CANopen server. Drawn from: inc/vortex/VortexHostSession.hpp VortexHostSession ; inc/vortex/VortexCanTransport.hpp VortexCanTransport ; inc/vortex/VortexProtocol.hpp NmtCommand ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . Layers ¶ Layer Files Role Session inc/vortex/VortexHostSession.hpp , src/VortexHostSession.cpp Encodes NMT and expedited SDO download frames; holds only a reference to the transport Protocol inc/vortex/VortexProtocol.hpp , inc/vortex/VortexCanFrame.hpp NmtCommand , object constants, the classic CAN frame type Transport interface inc/vortex/VortexCanTransport.hpp One pure-virtual method, send() Your transport your code Puts a VortexCanFrame on a real bus (BaseCan, SocketCAN) or records it (tests) One call through the layers ¶ sequenceDiagram participant App as Your code participant S as VortexHostSession participant T as Your transport participant C as CAN controller App->>S: sdoDownloadExpedited(5, 0x6060, 0, 3, 1) S->>S: size check, makeSdoDownload(): ID 0x605, 2F 60 60 00 03 00 00 00 S->>T: send(frame) T->>C: queue the frame (e.g. BaseCan::TrySendMessage) C-->>T: queued / queue full / bus-off T-->>App: true or false Design choices ¶ A virtual interface, not a template. The transport is a runtime object, like the BNO08x and TMC9660 transports elsewhere in HardFOC. One virtual call per frame is negligible next to the time an 8-byte frame takes on the wire (roughly 0.25 ms at 500 kbit/s). No heap, no threads, no RTOS. The session is one reference; frames are built on the stack. Transmit only. Receiving needs a thread or a callback, a filter and timeouts, which belong to the application or to a CANopen stack. The session stays a pure encoder. Same bytes as hf-utils-canopen. VortexCanFrame has the same fields as CanFrame in hf-utils-canopen , and the NMT and SDO download encodings are the same CiA 301 layouts, so a field-by-field copy converts between them. Where it sits in HardFOC ¶ Layer Repository Uses this driver for Driver collection hf-core-drivers Carries it as external/hf-vortex-driver CANopen glue hf-core handlers/common/canopen/ BaseCan links and the CANopenNode driver for the device side Device firmware hf-hal-vortex-v1 The Vortex board this driver talks to Next: API guide .

docs.text: Hardware ¶ The bus the driver talks on: settings, identifiers, the exact bytes of each frame and the objects it names. Bus settings ¶ Setting Value Frame format Classic CAN 2.0A: 11-bit identifier, no RTR, 0 to 8 data bytes ( VortexCanFrame ) Bit rate Set by your CAN controller, the same on every node; the Vortex V1 HAL uses 500 kbit/s Node IDs 1 to 127; NMT target 0 addresses every node Termination 120 Ω at each end of the bus Vortex V1 controller ESP32-C6 TWAI, TX on GPIO14, RX on GPIO15, transceiver standby on the PCAL95555 expander VortexCanFrame also carries extended and rtr flags; the session always sends them false. Identifiers ¶ Frame COB-ID Sent by this driver NMT command 0x000 Yes, sendNmt() SDO request (client to server) 0x600 + node Yes, sdoDownloadExpedited() SDO response (server to client) 0x580 + node No: read it yourself Boot-up and heartbeat 0x700 + node No EMCY 0x080 + node No PDOs (default set) 0x180 + node to 0x500 + node No NMT frame ¶ ID 0x000 , DLC 2. Byte Content 0 Command, from NmtCommand 1 Target node ID; 0 for all nodes Command Byte 0 NmtCommand::Start 0x01 NmtCommand::Stop 0x02 NmtCommand::PreOperational 0x80 NmtCommand::ResetNode 0x81 NmtCommand::ResetCommunication 0x82 SDO expedited download frame ¶ ID 0x600 + node , DLC 8, little-endian. Byte Content 0 Command specifier: 0x2F for 1 byte, 0x2B for 2 bytes, 0x23 for 4 bytes 1, 2 Index, low byte first 3 Sub-index 4 to 7 Value, low byte first; bytes past the size are 0 A size other than 1, 2 or 4 is refused before anything is sent. sequenceDiagram participant H as Host (VortexHostSession) participant N as Vortex node 5 H->>N: 0x000 01 05 (NMT start) Note over N: Operational H->>N: 0x605 2F 60 60 00 03 00 00 00 (0x6060:00 = 3) N-->>H: 0x585 60 60 60 00 00 00 00 00 (download confirmed) Note over H: the response is read by your code, not the session Object dictionary constants ¶ The named objects in VortexProtocol.hpp . The node's object dictionary (its EDS, or the CANopenNode tables in the device firmware) is authoritative. Constant Value Kind Header comment kIdxErrorRegister 0x1001 index CiA 301 — Error register (0x1001) subindex 0 kIdxPredefError 0x1003 index CiA 301 — Pre-defined error field (0x1003) sub 0 = number of errors kIdxErrorBehavior 0x1029 index CiA 301 — Error behavior (0x1029); sub 1 = communication error kIdxControlword 0x6040 index CiA 402 — Controlword (0x6040) — used for drive state machine kIdxStatusword 0x6041 index CiA 402 — Statusword (0x6041) kIdxModesOfOperation 0x6060 index CiA 402 — Modes of operation (0x6060) kIdxModesDisplay 0x6061 index CiA 402 — Modes of operation display (0x6061) kIdxPosActual 0x6064 index CiA 402 — Position actual value (0x6064) kIdxVelActual 0x606C index CiA 402 — Velocity actual value (0x606C) kIdxVendorBase 0x2000 index Proposed HardFOC vendor range 0x2000–0x2FFF, inside the CiA 301 manufacturer-specific area (0x2000–0x5FFF). Reserve sub-ranges as products solidify. kIdxVendorDeviceId 0x2000 index Example: 0x2000:01 — u32 build id / device magic (placeholder) kSubVendorDeviceId 0x01 sub-index Source: inc/vortex/VortexProtocol.hpp . tests/protocol checks every index and NMT command byte in this table against CiA 301 and CiA 402 at compile time ( Testing ). docs.text: Frame COB-ID Sent by this driver NMT command 0x000 Yes, sendNmt() SDO request (client to server) 0x600 + node Yes, sdoDownloadExpedited() SDO response (server to client) 0x580 + node No: read it yourself Boot-up and heartbeat 0x700 + node No EMCY 0x080 + node No PDOs (default set) 0x180 + node to 0x500 + node No

docs.text: ID 0x000 , DLC 2. Byte Content 0 Command, from NmtCommand 1 Target node ID; 0 for all nodes Command Byte 0 NmtCommand::Start 0x01 NmtCommand::Stop 0x02 NmtCommand::PreOperational 0x80 NmtCommand::ResetNode 0x81 NmtCommand::ResetCommunication 0x82
docs.title: NMT frame

docs.text: ID 0x600 + node , DLC 8, little-endian. Byte Content 0 Command specifier: 0x2F for 1 byte, 0x2B for 2 bytes, 0x23 for 4 bytes 1, 2 Index, low byte first 3 Sub-index 4 to 7 Value, low byte first; bytes past the size are 0 A size other than 1, 2 or 4 is refused before anything is sent. sequenceDiagram participant H as Host (VortexHostSession) participant N as Vortex node 5 H->>N: 0x000 01 05 (NMT start) Note over N: Operational H->>N: 0x605 2F 60 60 00 03 00 00 00 (0x6060:00 = 3) N-->>H: 0x585 60 60 60 00 00 00 00 00 (download confirmed) Note over H: the response is read by your code, not the session

docs.text: The named objects in VortexProtocol.hpp . The node's object dictionary (its EDS, or the CANopenNode tables in the device firmware) is authoritative. Constant Value Kind Header comment kIdxErrorRegister 0x1001 index CiA 301 — Error register (0x1001) subindex 0 kIdxPredefError 0x1003 index CiA 301 — Pre-defined error field (0x1003) sub 0 = number of errors kIdxErrorBehavior 0x1029 index CiA 301 — Error behavior (0x1029); sub 1 = communication error kIdxControlword 0x6040 index CiA 402 — Controlword (0x6040) — used for drive state machine kIdxStatusword 0x6041 index CiA 402 — Statusword (0x6041) kIdxModesOfOperation 0x6060 index CiA 402 — Modes of operation (0x6060) kIdxModesDisplay 0x6061 index CiA 402 — Modes of operation display (0x6061) kIdxPosActual 0x6064 index CiA 402 — Position actual value (0x6064) kIdxVelActual 0x606C index CiA 402 — Velocity actual value (0x606C) kIdxVendorBase 0x2000 index Proposed HardFOC vendor range 0x2000–0x2FFF, inside the CiA 301 manufacturer-specific area (0x2000–0x5FFF). Reserve sub-ranges as products solidify. kIdxVendorDeviceId 0x2000 index Example: 0x2000:01 — u32 build id / device magic (placeholder) kSubVendorDeviceId 0x01 sub-index Source: inc/vortex/VortexProtocol.hpp . tests/protocol checks every index and NMT command byte in this table against CiA 301 and CiA 402 at compile time ( Testing ).

docs.text: Porting ¶ Connect the driver to a CAN controller: the one method you implement, its contract, and a working adapter for HardFOC's BaseCan . The interface ¶ Method Called Must bool send(const VortexCanFrame& frame) noexcept Once per NMT or SDO call, from the caller's thread Queue or send the frame and return true, or return false; never throw That is the whole interface. The session calls it synchronously and passes its result back to your code. Rules for send() ¶ Copy the frame. It lives on the session's stack; do not keep the reference. Classic CAN. dlc is 0 to 8, extended and rtr are false for every frame the session builds. Send it as a classic (non-FD) frame. Decide on blocking. Return at once with false when the TX queue is full (the adapter below does), or block with a short timeout; either way, do not block forever. Report bus errors as false. Bus-off, controller not started, no acknowledgement: the caller retries or reports. Be thread-safe if you share it. Two sessions on one transport in two tasks call send() concurrently. Over BaseCan ¶ hf-internal-interface-wrap 's BaseCan is the CAN interface the HardFOC HALs expose ( EspCan on the ESP32-C6 TWAI today). Its hf_can_message_t holds FD-sized payloads; a classic frame uses the first 8 bytes. tests/docs/basecan_transport.cpp #include <cstring> #include "BaseCan.h" #include "vortex/VortexCanTransport.hpp" class BaseCanVortexTransport final : public hf :: vortex :: VortexCanTransport { public : explicit BaseCanVortexTransport ( BaseCan & can ) noexcept : can_ ( can ) {} bool send ( const hf :: vortex :: VortexCanFrame & frame ) noexcept override { if ( frame . dlc > 8 ) { return false ; // classic CAN only } hf_can_message_t msg {}; // classic frame: is_canfd = false msg . id = frame . id ; msg . is_extended = frame . extended ; msg . is_rtr = frame . rtr ; msg . dlc = frame . dlc ; std :: memcpy ( msg . data , frame . data , frame . dlc ); return can_ . TrySendMessage ( msg ) == hf_can_err_t :: CAN_SUCCESS ; // never blocks } private : BaseCan & can_ ; }; TrySendMessage() is SendMessage(message, 0) : it queues the frame or fails at once with CAN_ERR_QUEUE_FULL or CAN_ERR_BUS_OFF . On Vortex V1, CommChannelsManager::GetCanBus() returns the BaseCan* (null when the bus did not initialise). For tests ¶ A transport that records frames lets host tests check the exact bytes, as this repository's own check does: class LoopbackTransport final : public hf :: vortex :: VortexCanTransport { public : bool send ( const hf :: vortex :: VortexCanFrame & frame ) noexcept override { if ( count_ == kMaxFrames ) { return false ; // full: report a TX failure } frames_ [ count_ ++ ] = frame ; return true ; } std :: size_t count () const noexcept { return count_ ; } const hf :: vortex :: VortexCanFrame & frame ( std :: size_t i ) const noexcept { return frames_ [ i ]; } private : static constexpr std :: size_t kMaxFrames = 16 ; hf :: vortex :: VortexCanFrame frames_ [ kMaxFrames ]{}; std :: size_t count_ = 0 ; }; How to check a port ¶ Run examples/generic on the host and note the two frames it checks. Send the same calls through your transport and watch the bus with an analyser: IDs 0x000 and 0x601 , the bytes in Hardware . Disconnect the bus (no acknowledgement) and check that send() eventually returns false rather than hanging. Next: Examples .

docs.text: Quickstart ¶ Connect a host to a Vortex node, write the transport, and start the node in a CiA 402 mode in about 15 lines. A started drive can move the motor NmtCommand::Start puts the node in Operational, and the CiA 402 enable sequence powers the motor. Clamp the rotor or remove the load until you have checked the node ID and the objects you write. Wiring ¶ Host Vortex V1 Notes CAN_H CAN_H Twisted pair with CAN_L CAN_L CAN_L GND GND A common reference for the transceivers 120 Ω termination 120 Ω termination One at each end of the bus, none in between The bit rate must match on every node: 500 kbit/s is what the Vortex V1 HAL configures. See Hardware . Add the driver ¶ git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-vortex-driver.git external/hf-vortex-driver add_subdirectory ( external/hf-vortex-driver ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE hf_vortex_driver ) The transport ¶ The driver calls one method of yours, send() . For a first test on a PC, record the frames instead of sending them: tests/docs/loopback_transport.hpp class LoopbackTransport final : public hf :: vortex :: VortexCanTransport { public : bool send ( const hf :: vortex :: VortexCanFrame & frame ) noexcept override { if ( count_ == kMaxFrames ) { return false ; // full: report a TX failure } frames_ [ count_ ++ ] = frame ; return true ; } std :: size_t count () const noexcept { return count_ ; } const hf :: vortex :: VortexCanFrame & frame ( std :: size_t i ) const noexcept { return frames_ [ i ]; } private : static constexpr std :: size_t kMaxFrames = 16 ; hf :: vortex :: VortexCanFrame frames_ [ kMaxFrames ]{}; std :: size_t count_ = 0 ; }; On a board, wrap your CAN driver instead: Porting has a ten-line adapter over BaseCan . Start a node ¶ tests/docs/quickstart.cpp #include "vortex/VortexHostSession.hpp" #include "vortex/VortexProtocol.hpp" using namespace hf :: vortex ; // Put node 5 in Operational and select CiA 402 profile velocity mode (3). bool start_node_in_velocity_mode ( VortexCanTransport & bus ) { VortexHostSession session ( bus ); constexpr std :: uint8_t kNode = 5 ; if ( ! session . sendNmt ( NmtCommand :: Start , kNode )) { // 0x000: 01 05 return false ; // transport refused the frame } return session . sdoDownloadExpedited ( kNode , kIdxModesOfOperation , // 0x605: 2F 60 60 00 03 /*sub=*/ 0 , /*value=*/ 3 , /*size=*/ 1 ); } What each step does ¶ Step Frame on the bus Effect on the node VortexHostSession session(bus) none Binds the session to your transport; no state, no allocation sendNmt(NmtCommand::Start, 5) ID 0x000 , 2 bytes: 01 05 Node 5 enters Operational sdoDownloadExpedited(5, 0x6060, 0, 3, 1) ID 0x605 , 8 bytes: 2F 60 60 00 03 00 00 00 Writes 3 (profile velocity) to modes of operation Both calls return true when your transport accepted the frame. They do not wait for the node: the SDO response ( 0x585 ) is yours to read if you need the confirmation. If it does not work ¶ Symptom Check send() returns false The controller is bus-off or its TX queue is full: check termination, bit rate and that another node acknowledges Frames leave, the node does nothing Wrong node ID; the node is still booting (wait for its boot-up message 0x700 + node ) SDO abort ( 0x580 + node , byte 0 0x80 ) The object does not exist or is read-only on that node; check its EDS Nothing on the bus at all Transceiver in standby (on Vortex V1 the standby line is on the PCAL95555 expander) Next: Hardware .

docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: on the host, on every pull request, without hardware. Host checks ¶ Check Command Covers Generic example cmake -B build -S examples/generic && cmake --build build && ./build/vortex_driver_generic_check NMT start and an SDO write through a loopback transport Protocol constants cmake -B build-tests -S . -DHF_VORTEX_BUILD_TESTS=ON && cmake --build build-tests && ctest --test-dir build-tests Every index and NMT command byte in VortexProtocol.hpp against CiA 301 / CiA 402 ( static_assert , so a wrong value fails the build), and the SDO frame for error behaviour 0x1029:01 Documentation frames cmake -B build-docs -S . -DHF_VORTEX_BUILD_DOC_SNIPPETS=ON && cmake --build build-docs && ctest --test-dir build-docs Every snippet on this site compiles with -Wall -Wextra -Werror , and check_frames compares each frame it sends with the bytes the pages show tests/docs/check_frames.cpp checks the NMT and SDO frames of the Quickstart, the broadcast NMT, the 1-, 2- and 4-byte SDO writes, the refusal of size 3 and the CiA 402 enable sequence. CI workflows ¶ Workflow What it checks Host generic test ( ci-generic.yml ) Builds and runs the generic example, then builds the documentation code (with the BaseCan adapter against hf-internal-interface-wrap main ) and the protocol test, and runs both Docs ( ci-docs-publish.yml ) Strict site build, figure and generated-table drift, Doxygen, offline link check, Lighthouse budget; publishes the site from main The docs workflow calls the shared, versioned workflow of hf-general-ci-tools . On hardware ¶ There is no hardware test in this repository. Check a port as described in Porting , with a bus analyser.

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms, causes and fixes, cheapest check first. Symptom Cause Fix sdoDownloadExpedited() returns false, nothing on the bus size is not 1, 2 or 4 Use the size of the object's type Every call returns false Your send() fails: controller not started, bus-off, TX queue full Check the controller is initialised, termination (60 Ω between CAN_H and CAN_L with power off), bit rate Frames on the bus, error frames follow No other node acknowledges, or bit rates differ Power the node; set the same bit rate everywhere (500 kbit/s on Vortex V1) Node ignores NMT Wrong node ID, or the node has not finished booting Wait for its boot-up message ( 0x700 + node , one byte 0x00 ); check the ID SDO abort from the node ( 0x580 + node , byte 0 0x80 ) Object missing, read-only, wrong size or value out of range Bytes 4 to 7 hold the CiA 301 abort code; check the EDS CiA 402 drive does not reach Operation enabled A command was sent before the previous state was reached, or the drive is in Fault Read the statusword ( 0x6041 ) between steps; send Fault reset ( 0x0080 ) first Motor does not move although enabled Mode of operation not set, or no target written Write 0x6060 and the target object for that mode Next: API reference .

The session encodes CANopen NMT and expedited SDO download frames as VortexCanFrame values and hands each to the VortexCanTransport interface (its pure-virtual methods are listed from inc/vortex/VortexCanTransport.hpp). Your transport class implements that interface with BaseCan, SocketCAN or a test loopback, and puts the frame on a classic CAN bus. The Vortex device on the bus is the CANopen server.
